result.topic_en: Euler explains that the variation of the integral formula ∫Z dx is the increment it receives when y, viewed as a function of x and t, is increased by dt(dy/dt), and expresses this variation as dt∫dx(dZ/dt) in terms of N, P, Q, R.
result.transcription:
440 METHODVS NOVA CALCVLVM
endoque ipsarum $x$, $y$, $p$, $q$, $r$ etc. ita vt per diffe-
rentiationem ordinariam habeatur:
$dZ = M dx + N dy + P dp + Q dq + R dr$ ,
vbi quidem hactenus nulla ratio nouae variabilis $t$
est habita atque integratio formulae propositae $\int Z dx$
per solam variabilem $x$ est expedienda, quo obser-
vato, quaestio huc redit, vt si iam $y$ vt functio
binarum variabilium $x$ et $t$ consideretur et vbique
quantitas $y$ elemento $dt(\frac{dy}{dt})$ augeatur, augmentum
quod ipsa formula integralis $\int Z dx$ inde capiet de-
finiatur, hoc enim augmentum ipsa erit variatio
formulae integralis propositae.

10. Quare ad hanc variationem inueniendam
in functione illa Z vbique loco $y$ scribatur eius valor
auctus $y + dt(\frac{dy}{dt})$, sicque vt ante vidimus, ipsa
functio Z augmentum capiet $dt(\frac{dZ}{dt})$ ex quo ipsa
formula integralis augmentum capiet hoc: $\int dt(\frac{dZ}{dt})dx$,
quod erit ipsa variatio quaesita. Quoniam vero in
hac integratione sola $x$ pro variabili habetur, ele-
mentum $dt$ ante signum poni poterit ita vt iam
variatio futura sit $= dt \int dx (\frac{dZ}{dt})$.

11. Quoniam igitur in § 8 valor ipsius $(\frac{dZ}{dt})$
iam euolutus habetur si ille hic substituatur formu-
lae $\int Z dx$ variatio prodibit ita expressa:
$dt \int dx (N(\frac{dy}{dt}) + P(\frac{ddy}{dx\,dt}) + Q(\frac{d^3y}{dx^2dt}) + R(\frac{d^4y}{dx^3.dt})$ etc.)

items.english: the question comes down to this: if y is now considered as a function of the two variables x and t, and the quantity y is everywhere increased by the element dt(dy/dt), the increment which the integral formula ∫Z dx thereby receives is to be determined

items.quote:
hoc enim augmentum ipsa erit variatio
formulae integralis propositae.
items.english: for this increment will be the variation itself of the proposed integral formula.

variatio futura sit $= dt \int dx (\frac{dZ}{dt})$.
items.english: the element dt can be placed before the integral sign, so that the variation will now be dt ∫dx (dZ/dt).
